kitDescription: Red Hood is an Iron SR Attacker with the game's only Λ burst, so she can fill any burst slot and her burst does something different depending on which step she is on. Step 1 (Beast Cage) gives the whole team a flat attack boost scaled off her own ATK plus a team DEF grant, and refunds her own 40-second burst cooldown once per battle. Step 2 (The Last Howl) is purely defensive — she taunts all enemies, amplifies healing she receives, lifesteals a share of her attack damage, and refunds her cooldown a second time. Step 3 (Red Wolf) is her damage window: for 10 seconds she swaps to a different weapon that hits for 51.46% of final ATK per shot with a 250% full-charge multiplier and fires far faster, while she also gains +71.42% ATK and wider pierce. Passively she pierces for the whole fight, builds charge speed as she shoots (3.81% per shot, up to 10 stacks), and converts any charge speed above the +100% cap into charge damage at 240% — which in practice only pays out during Red Wolf, when the +100.8% charge-speed buff pushes her past the cap.

redAssertions: S1b 'the Red Wolf +100.8% charge speed is ALSO converted' — blind expected an effective chargeDamage tier in [150,400] (241.92 = 2.4x100.8, or 333.36 = 2.4x138.9); driver ships 90. ADJUDICATED RECON_ERROR: game-mechanics.md §4 states the conversion is of charge speed past the +100% CAP ('Red Hood S1: excess x 2.4 -> Charge Damage'), so the faithful excess is (100.8+38.1-100)x2.4 = 93.36, not 241.92/333.36. The blind's sibling assertion (band [40,110]) PASSED against the driver's 90.

B3 'Charge Speed +100.8% rides the same window' — blind required an explicit buffApply chargeSpeedPct 100.8; the driver folds it into weaponSwap.chargeTimeSec 0.3. ADJUDICATED RECON_ERROR (equivalent encoding): CS is subtractive on charge time and hard-capped at +100%, so 138.9% total floors the swap charge and cadence becomes rate-of-fire-gated at 200 rpm = 18 frames; the buff is co-terminous with the swap (both 10s from the same cast) so it can have no observable effect outside it.
Adapted blind run (2 intent-preserving RECON_ERROR corrections): 30 passed / 0 failed / 6 skipped = convergence GREEN.

verdictRationale: All 14 kit lines are FAITHFUL (9) or DOCUMENTED_GAP (5); there are no silent drops, no wrong buckets, and no divergence from any number the prose itself states. The two blind S5 REDs are both RECON_ERROR and I confirmed that independently rather than on the driver's word: RED 1 is refuted by the repo's own SSOT (game-mechanics.md §4 names this exact kit line and defines the excess as charge speed past the +100% CAP, which makes 241.92/333.36 arithmetically wrong and the driver's zero-out-of-burst behavior correct — notably the blind's own always-on 36.6 passive limb is the over-credit here), and RED 2 is an equivalent encoding forced by the subtractive, +100%-capped charge-speed model, observable through the pinned 18-frame in-window cadence. The adapted blind run is 30/0/6 green, so convergence holds once the two misreads are corrected, and blind S6 independently reproduces every other load-bearing encoding including the caster-relative casterAtkPct routing and the two per-step burstCdr refunds. The one real defect is minor and bookkeeping-only (the conversion line double-entered as both modeled and unmodeled). The blocking-adjacent finding is discrimination, which I mark FALSE: the Step-1 and Step-2 burst-cooldown refunds are load-bearing rotation economy (each is a full reset of her exactly-40s cooldown, and together they chain her Λ steps 1->2->3 early), yet the driver ships zero assertion for them on the stated grounds that the engine emits no burstCdr event — but a removal counterfactual is trivially available and observable in the very channels the driver's test already reads (her burstCast count, stage-3 window count, and total damage), so 'not cleanly isolable' overstates the difficulty. That is a test-coverage gap, not a faithfulness bug, so it does not block GO; it is the top follow-up. Same-model residual for the owner to spot-check: every agent in this chain is Claude and all three converged on treating the S1 conversion as a static stand-in gated to Red Wolf — the shipped 90 and the reviewer's 93.36 are both unmeasured point estimates of a genuinely dynamic quantity, and the unit's known COLD ~0.867 residual most plausibly lives there, so a full-charge popup pair inside vs outside Red Wolf (holding ATK constant, backing out damagePct 51.46 / chargeMultPct 250 / atkPct 71.42) is the measurement that would settle it. Second spot-check: both blind agents independently asked for the Last Howl lifesteal to emit recovery events for on-recovery consumers — harmless today with no HP pool, but it is the one deliberate omission two independent re-derivations both flagged.
